name: erdtree
description: Multi-threaded file-tree visualizer and disk usage analyzer

repo.name: erdtree
repo.description: A modern, cross-platform, multi-threaded, and general purpose filesystem and disk-usage utility that is aware of .gitignore and hidden file rules.

readme.summary: Excellent clarity on what the tool does, but completely missing installation instructions, practical examples, and any quick-start guidance beyond the comprehensive help text.
readme.top_issue: No installation instructions provided despite this being a Homebrew package - users don't know how to install it (e.g., 'brew install erdtree')

injection_risks.description: The function `read_config_to_string` reads a configuration file from various locations, but it does not validate the contents of the file. This could potentially lead to command injection if an attacker can modify the configuration file.
The function `parse` constructs a vector of command-line arguments from a TOML configuration. If an attacker can modify the TOML file, they could potentially inject malicious commands.

critical_findings: Potential command injection vulnerability in configuration file handling
security.summary: The code has some security concerns, including potential command injection vulnerabilities and lack of input validation, but no critical secrets or error exposure issues were found.

common_complaints: Performance issues with level/depth limiting (indexing whole tree unnecessarily)
Critical bugs causing crashes and panics (sudo panic, SIGSEGV)
Missing common features compared to tree command (exclude patterns, case-insensitive sorting)
Terminal state not restored after crashes
sentiment.summary: erdtree shows signs of maintenance neglect with multiple unaddressed bugs, zero comments on issues, and feature requests spanning 18+ months without responses, indicating slow or unresponsive project stewardship.

communication.summary: The maintainer is generally helpful and patient, but could improve with more detailed explanations and quicker responses.
